### Description of Amazon SMS pricing

* * *

**The following is the official introduction to SMS charging!

For more details, please visit the official link.

https://aws.amazon.com/sns/sms-pricing/

Worldwide SMS pricing
================

With Amazon SNS, you can send SMS (text) messages to more than 200 countries/regions and for various use cases such as Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and one-time passwords (OTP). Amazon SNS has no upfront fees; you pay as you go. With Amazon SNS, you can also tag SMS messages as transactional or promotional based on the use case and the content of the message. To learn more about message types, see the FAQs.

**Important:**
The price of sending SMS messages varies by country/region and region; in some cases, the price also differs between carriers in the same country/region, depending on the carrier of the destination phone number. The prices provided below are for reference only and change frequently. After sending some messages, you can use the daily usage report to obtain the exact price of each message (in USD).

* * *

SMS originating identities
--------

When sending SMS with Amazon SNS, depending on the destination country/region, you will need to purchase and use a dedicated originating identity. For more information, see Originating identities for SMS in the Amazon SNS documentation. For country/region-specific requirements that must be observed when sending SMS, see the special requirements pages for India and the United States.

**Important**: To use any of the supported originating identities, you must purchase an originating phone number using the Amazon Pinpoint console. You pay according to the resource types described below. After you purchase and activate the phone number, you can use it as an originating ID in Amazon SNS to send SMS messages to your recipients.

#### Dedicated long codes

A long code is a standard phone number used to send SMS messages (a 10-digit number in many countries/regions). Sometimes a long code is not required to send SMS, because each country/region supports different types of SMS originating identities. You can use a dedicated long code in Amazon SNS by registering it in the Amazon Pinpoint console. For instructions on how to purchase and use a long code, see Request a long code in the Amazon SNS documentation.

#### 10-digit dedicated long code (10DLC)

10DLC is a 10-digit phone number used in the United States. To use a 10DLC number, you need to register your company and create a 10DLC campaign through the Amazon Pinpoint console. After that, you can associate the 10DLC number with the 10DLC campaign. For more information, see the 10DLC page.

The registration and monthly fees payable when using 10DLC are as follows.

1. Company registration: a one-time fee of 4 USD per company
2. 10DLC campaign registration: a one-time fee of 50 USD for T-Mobile registration. This fee may be waived without notice.
3. 10DLC campaign monthly fee: 10 USD for each approved regular 10DLC campaign, 2 USD for each approved low-traffic 10DLC campaign.
4. 10DLC phone number monthly fee: 1 USD for each 10DLC phone number.

After registering a 10DLC number and activating your account using the Amazon Pinpoint console, you can use this number as a valid originating ID for sending SMS with Amazon SNS.

#### Toll-free numbers (TFN)

A toll-free number is a 10-digit number beginning with any of the following three-digit codes: 800, 888, 877, 866, 855, 844 or 833. In the United States, Amazon SNS currently only supports SMS-capable toll-free numbers. You can purchase a toll-free number on the Amazon Pinpoint console at a monthly rental price of 2 USD.

#### Dedicated short codes

Amazon SNS supports dedicated short codes. A short code is a short number sequence used to send SMS messages (3 to 8 digits, depending on the country or region). Short codes are easier to enter and remember than traditional phone numbers. In some countries/regions, short codes improve the message delivery rate. You can purchase short codes for multiple different countries and regions directly through AWS. To obtain pricing information or apply for a dedicated short code for other countries/regions, create a case in the AWS Support Center. For more information, visit our short code documentation.

For countries/regions where short codes are frequently requested, see the pricing below.

| Country/Region | One-time setup fee | Monthly fee | Estimated provisioning time** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| United States | 650 USD | 995 USD | 12 weeks |
| Canada | 3000 USD | 995 USD | 16 weeks |
| United Kingdom | 0 USD | 1500 USD | 16 weeks |
| Japan | 1750 USD | 1150 USD | 12 weeks |
| India* | 150 USD | 300 USD | 3 weeks |
| China | 15 USD | 15 USD | 3 weeks |
| Brazil | 330 USD | 330 USD | 4 weeks |
| Others | Please create a support case to check the price | | |

\* Only ILDO traffic is supported.

\*\* The provisioning time starts when: 1) all the information and documents required by the carrier have been submitted, and 2) the carrier has no other feedback or changes required. The provisioning time does not start counting after the initial request is made. Amazon provides feedback on your submission so that it meets the general carrier feedback requirements. After all Amazon feedback has been processed according to the general carrier standards, the short code application will be sent to the mobile carriers. Each mobile carrier evaluates the application separately through its own review/approval process. Carriers may require additional information or ask you to change the short code application or the model provided. The estimated carrier provisioning time is only a guide based on past schedules and is not guaranteed for future registration events, because some short codes may take longer to provision, depending on the use case and/or carrier feedback. Some mobile carriers have routine provisioning freezes and may extend and delay the carrier provisioning schedule; customers should confirm whether their country/region has a provisioning freeze during their registration period to confirm the impact on their schedule. Amazon does not have the ability to escalate or expedite the short code provisioning schedule, which is the cumulative result of schedules and non-overlapping processes owned by each mobile carrier. If a mobile carrier considers the short code application non-compliant, it reserves the right to reject the application, which may further delay the provisioning time. A short code may need to be approved for use on certain carrier networks before it can be used on other carrier networks; however, the short code will not be provisioned for your account until all carriers have completed approval. Adding or modifying use cases for all short code campaigns must be communicated to the carriers through the short code application process and may follow the same schedule. Failing to communicate changes to the short code use case may result in the short code being suspended.

_**Note**: After you create a short code application case, we will send you information about the one-time and recurring fees for obtaining the short code for the country or region you applied for. If you accept these fees, fees related to the use of the short code will be incurred immediately. You are responsible for paying these fees even if the short code you applied for has not been fully provisioned._

For enterprise customers, please consult your AWS technical account manager directly for onboarding and further assistance.
